author: John Wagner
title: Snappers look to regain edge that carried them in '25 - NewsBreak
text:
By John Wagner ,
9 hours ago
Last year the Braham Snappers had one of the team’s best seasons in recent memory, finishing with a 10-11 overall record and posting a 6-9 mark that was good for fifth place in the Eastern Minny League’s eight-team North Division.
This year, well, things have been a little tougher.
The Snappers are still searching for their first win this season and are 0-9 in the North Division.
“We had a lot of confidence, a lot of belief that we could come back and build on last season,” said assistant coach Andy Beckstrom. “We saw that next level of development in some of our younger guys, and we saw the commitment, the involvement that you need.
“This year, we’ve had some of the [previous] struggles: getting consistency to have everyone show up, and playing with confidence and consistency.”
Braham has shown glimpses of that previous success, though. For example, the Snappers were tied with Isanti 3-3 through six innings on June 28, only to see the Redbirds fly to a 9-3 victory thanks to two runs in the seventh and four more in the ninth.
The Snappers are led by the Johnsons. Jesse Johnson has a 4.85 ERA, while Jonah Johnson has a misleading 6.75 ERA after holding Isanti in check through seven innings. He also limited Ogilvie to two earned runs in eight innings on May 31, a game the Snappers lost 5-4.
Offensively Jacob Johnson has the team’s lone home run this season and leads the team with seven hits, two more than Jesse Johnson and Logan Leniz.
“Jonah has stepped up and pitched well for us this year,” Beckstrom said. “Jesse has pitched very well for us as well, and Jake and Jared have been a consistent veteran presence.
“They also provide leadership in the dugout, helping our younger players learn the nuances of the game.”
Among the younger players who are playing important roles on the team are Landon Mold, Elliot Blatz and Leniz.
The Snappers return to action with a pair of critical home games. The team will host Nowthen on Saturday, July 11 in a 4 p.m. start, then host Ham Lake the next afternoon, with first pitch set for 2 p.m.
Nowthen also is winless in the Eastern Minny League this season, while Ham Lake’s lone victory is against Nowthen.
“We’re going to be OK; we’ve just been running a gauntlet of tough teams,” Beckstrom said. “We’ve not seen any pitching until we took the field to start the season, and we’re facing some really good pitchers.”
He added that perhaps the key to the team’s return to last year’s form is to rekindle the excitement of playing baseball.
“We want to feel those feelings that made us want to play Town Ball in the first place,” Beckstrom said. “We have a chance to be competitive; we want to remind our guys about the things that we can do well.
“There are teams that are going to be in a one-game playoff to make the regional tournament, and we want to try to avoid that. If we can win some of those games we’re playing this month, that will improve our chances of avoiding those play-in games.”
